acquisition method: we interrogated the spleen proteome using a label-free shotgun approach
alkylation reagent: Alkylation was achieved using iodoacetamide (GE Healthcare, Little Chalfont, Buckinghamshire, UK)
alkylation concentration: iodoacetamide (GE Healthcare, Little Chalfont, Buckinghamshire, UK) to a final concentration of 9.4 mM
cleavage agent: digestion with MS grade trypsin (Promega, Madison, WI, USA)
collision energy: fragmented by Higher Energy Collision Induced Dissociation (HCD) with a stepped Normalized Collisional Energy (NCE) of 28–30
fragmentation method: fragmented by Higher Energy Collision Induced Dissociation (HCD)
instrument: The spectral data was acquired using a Q Exactive mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific®, Bremen, Germany)
labeling: we interrogated the spleen proteome using a label-free shotgun approach
reduction reagent: proteins were reduced using dithiothreitol (Sigma Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA)
reduction concentration: dithiothreitol (Sigma Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA) to a final concentration of 3.3 mM
